brief: A color palette generator that works like a musical instrument — play colors, harmonies lock like chords

dominant_strengths: Conceptual metaphor of piano-keys-as-color-generator is genuinely novel and links music theory to color theory elegantly
Clear hierarchy between palette display and keyboard input zones, with consistent dark canvas letting swatches pop
Chord-type modifiers (Major/Minor/Diminished/Augmented) extend the metaphor with real semantic payload
dominant_weaknesses: Massive vertical dead space between palette cards and keyboard leaves the composition feeling unbalanced and underpopulated
Swatches use generic rounded rectangles with no visual cue tying them to the pressed key — the 'chord lock' moment is invisible
Typography is utilitarian system sans with weak hierarchy; hex labels and role tags compete instead of nesting
fix_priorities: Tighten vertical rhythm: pull palette closer to keyboard or add a staff/waveform visualization bridging them
Add a visible chord-lock animation — connecting lines, ripple, or harmonic glow from key to swatch
Refine typography with a display face for hex codes and clearer role-label demotion
Differentiate selected key state more dramatically so the instrument feels responsive and alive
rationale.norman_balance: Reflective concept outshines visceral polish and behavioral feedback, leaving the metaphor intellectually clear but emotionally muted.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially fits — the keyboard-to-palette mapping exists, but the 'chords locking' moment lacks the visual/motion craft to feel instrumental.
